questions.q: Which of these are jobs done by an operating system? Tick all that apply.
options: Writing the programs the user runs
questions.feedback: Five management jobs plus the interface. Compressing a file is a utility, and the operating system does not write anybody's programs.

questions.q: State what is meant by systems software.

markPoints.concept: software that runs and manages the computer itself, rather than doing a job for the user
markPoints.exemplar: Software that runs and manages the computer itself.

questions.example: Software that runs and manages the computer itself, such as the operating system and utilities, rather than application software that does a job for the user.
questions.paraphrase: Programs that control and look after the machine rather than carrying out a task for the person using it.
questions.feedback: Managing the computer. Naming examples without saying what they do is half an answer.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.5 Lesson 1 — Control room, station 2: What the OS does

questions.q: Match each kind of user interface to a situation it suits.
pairs: A pupil using a laptop to write an essay
A technician writing a script to set up fifty machines at once
A cash machine with a few fixed choices
A driver who needs their hands on the wheel
questions.feedback: Each interface suits a different balance of ease and control.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.5 Lesson 1 — Control room, station 3: Graphical user interface

questions.q: Explain why a technician might prefer a command line interface to a graphical one.

markPoints.concept: commands can be combined into a script and run automatically
markPoints.exemplar: Commands can be written into a script and run automatically.

markPoints.concept: so a long or repeated job is done far faster than clicking through it
accept: faster|quicker|less time|saves time|far more|more efficient|without clicking|no clicking|one go
markPoints.exemplar: This means a repeated job is done far faster than clicking through a graphical interface.

questions.example: A command line lets commands be written into a script and run automatically, so a job that has to be repeated across fifty machines is done in one go rather than by clicking through the same windows fifty times.
questions.paraphrase: Typed commands can be saved into a script and executed without supervision, which means a repetitive task finishes far more quickly than working through menus would allow.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.5 Lesson 1 — Control room, station 3: Graphical user interface

questions.q: Explain one disadvantage of a command line interface for an ordinary user.

markPoints.concept: the user has to know the commands
markPoints.exemplar: The user has to know the exact commands.

markPoints.concept: so it is harder to learn and a mistyped command may do something unintended
markPoints.exemplar: This makes it much harder to learn than clicking on an icon.

questions.example: A command line gives no clues: the user has to know the exact command and type it correctly, so it is much harder to learn than pointing at an icon, and one mistyped command can do real damage.
questions.paraphrase: Nothing on the screen tells you what is available, so you must already know the commands and type them exactly, which makes it far harder to pick up than clicking on pictures.
questions.feedback: What the user must know, and what follows from not knowing it.
